samples.summary: Durable Yorkie client key is deterministic (`wb:{userId}:{docKey}`) while `ActivateClient`/`DeactivateClient` are authorized on token validity alone — any valid Yorkie token can hijack or tear down another user's per-document client row
samples.evidence:
`durableClientKey()` builds the Yorkie `ClientOptions.key` as `wb:${userId}:${docKey}` (durable-session.ts:80-82). Both inputs are readily obtainable: `userId` is the sequential numeric `me.id`, published to every workspace member via `WorkspaceMember.user.id` (packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:23), and `docKey` is `sheet-<documentId>` / `doc-<id>` etc., with `documentId` visible in URLs and listings. The key is passed straight through `CollabDocumentProvider` -> `DurableYorkieProvider` -> `KeyedYorkieProvider` as `clientKey` (collab-document-provider.tsx, durable-yorkie-provider.tsx).

Yorkie identifies a client row by `(projectID, clientKey)` upsert — that is precisely the property this feature relies on for a reload to resume the same actor. But the auth webhook binds nothing: `CLIENT_METHODS = new Set(['ActivateClient','DeactivateClient'])` and `if (CLIENT_METHODS.has(method)) return ALLOW;` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:69, 246-248), documented as "No document. Validate token only" (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:82). Nothing compares the token's `sub` against the requested client key.

Attack: obtain any valid Yorkie token — `GET /auth/yorkie-token` with any account, or the fully public `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` with any share link (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:87-95, no session required). The project public key (`VITE_YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY`) and `VITE_YORKIE_RPC_ADDR` ship in the bundle. Then `new Client({apiKey, authTokenInjector, key: 'wb:<victimId>:<sheet-docId>'}).activate()` seizes the victim's client row, and `.deactivate()` tears it down server-side. The victim's durable client then shares/loses its actor and checkpoint state — the exact `clientSeq` collision and actor-keyed pull-dedup failure the design itself names as "silent edit loss" — and with the store attached this drives the SDK's `LocalChangesDropped` (`actor-mismatch` / `document-purged`) paths, discarding the victim's unsent offline work.

Before this change the client key was a random per-session value, so this was unreachable. I could not verify Yorkie server's exact `ActivateClient` upsert semantics from this repo, hence medium confidence; the feature's own resume guarantee depends on that behaviour.

samples.summary: `NonDurableScope` does not cover the share route's PDF branch — it returns before the wrapper, leaving that path protected only by the separate `pdf-` docKey exclusion the design plans to remove
samples.evidence:
`SharedDocumentInner` returns early for PDFs at lines 967-980 (`if (kind === 'pdf') return <SharedPdfLayout .../>`), well before the `<NonDurableScope>` wrapper that begins at line 1016. `SharedPdfLayout` reaches `PdfCollabProvider`, which mounts `CollabDocumentProvider` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:199) — i.e. a share-link view whose subtree has `useDurabilityPermitted() === true`.

Today that is saved only by a second, unrelated mechanism: `isExcluded(docKey)` returning true for the `pdf-` prefix (packages/frontend/src/lib/use-durable-document.ts:40-42), matching `docKey={`pdf-${documentId}`}` at pdf-collab.tsx:200. The design states the `pdf-` exclusion exists solely because PDFs have no sync chip and is to be lifted "until it has a chip" (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md, § Who gets it). The moment that exclusion is removed, a **signed-in** visitor on somebody else's PDF share link gets the durable branch: their own `wb:{userId}:pdf-{id}` client authenticated with `fetchYorkieToken` (their personal token) instead of the share token whose role and expiry the webhook validates, writing the shared document's comment content to a disk that outlives the link's revocation — the precise harm `NonDurableScope` was added to prevent. The new test `shared-document-durability.test.tsx` never exercises the PDF branch, so nothing detects the regression.

samples.summary: Recovery offer runs even when the access reconcile failed, so archived content from a workspace the user was removed from can be materialized into a new server-side document they own
samples.evidence:
`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` is the only mechanism that removes content from the *victim's* device after somebody else revokes access (offline-erase.ts:334-341 documents this). In `OfflineRuntime`, the reconcile is wrapped in `try { const accessible = await fetchDocuments(); ... } catch (err) { console.warn(...) }` (offline-runtime.tsx:114-142) and control then falls through to `offerRecoverableWork(...)` at line 150. The new test `'keeps sweeping when the reconcile fails'` (offline-runtime.test.tsx) explicitly asserts the recovery toast still appears after `fetchDocuments` rejects.

So on any session where the listing fails (offline, transient 5xx, the 401 arm throwing `AuthExpiredError`), an archive belonging to a workspace the user has been removed from is offered, and accepting it calls `recoverOfflineCopy` -> `createDocument({title, type})` + `applyImportedContent` (lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts), turning a local remnant into a permanent server-side document the removed user owns. The design's stated rule is that "content must not outlive the authority to read it", and `purgeDocument({archives:'drop'})` exists precisely so a revoked archive cannot be re-materialized. The offer should be gated on a reconcile that actually succeeded. Confidence is medium because the user already possesses the plaintext locally; the escalation is that it becomes a durable server-side copy.

samples.summary: Path-traversal regression test weakened from "every request URL carries the encoded id" to "some request does"
samples.evidence: The positive half of the traversal guard changed from a per-URL `expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL))` inside the loop to a single `expect(paths.some(p => p.includes(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL)))).toBe(true)` (url.test.ts:170-174). For `deleteWorkspace`, the `some()` is now satisfied by the companion `fetchWorkspace`/`fetchDocuments` requests that `documentIdsIn` added (api/workspaces.ts:101-115) rather than by the DELETE itself, so the DELETE's own id handling is no longer positively asserted. The `not.toContain('/auth/logout')` check is still per-path and still catches a raw `../../auth/logout`, which is why this is minor rather than a hole — but the suite's stated purpose is "this pins the whole client" (url.test.ts:73), and a call site that mangles the id in any way that is not a dot-segment traversal now passes silently. Restoring per-request strictness (e.g. asserting on the request that matches the route being named) would keep the original coverage.

samples.summary: SDK store keys — which embed the Yorkie project API key and the signed-in user's numeric id — are interpolated into exception messages that reach `console.warn` and `onWriteFailure`
samples.evidence: `refuseIfDisabled` builds `new DOMException(`offline saving is switched off; "${docKey}" is not being stored`, ...)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:384-387) and `refuseIfEvicted` does the same at 715-718. `docKey` here is the SDK's scoped store key `apiKey/clientKey/docKey`, i.e. `<yorkie project apiKey>/wb:<userId>:<docKey>/<docKey>`. These errors are handed to `onWriteFailure` (line 1307/1318) and, on other paths, logged verbatim by `console.warn('[offline] ...', err)` in offline-erase.ts:258/293/327/409 and offline-runtime.tsx:109/141/154. The Yorkie key involved is the *public* project key so the disclosure is low-impact, but it pairs the project key with a user id and a document id in browser console output and in anything that ships console errors to a log sink. Logging the bare `documentKeyOf(docKey)` would carry the same diagnostic value without the identifiers.

samples.summary: `collectStale` deletes other accounts' live entries and archives on a shared device, with no identity scoping, on a sweep triggered by whoever is signed in
samples.evidence: `collectStale` walks `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` with no `BY_USER` intersection (line 1129) and calls `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` with `onlyUser` omitted (line 1143), so one signed-in account's once-per-session sweep (`OfflineRuntime`, offline-runtime.tsx:107) destroys any other account's entries and archives on the same origin. The comments at 1106-1124 argue this is deliberate — a departed user's content would otherwise never be collected — and `evictOldest`/`listArchives`/`loadArchive` do stay scoped, so this is destruction rather than disclosure. It is still a cross-tenant destructive action initiated by an unrelated principal, and an archive is by this feature's own design the *only* copy of work the server never took; worth an explicit acceptance rather than leaving it to the reader to reconcile against `dropAllForUser`'s careful scoping two methods above.

samples.summary: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` falls back to a possibly stale `localStorage` identity, so a sign-out from a route the authenticated shell never mounted can erase the wrong account and leave the current user's content on a shared disk
samples.evidence: `offlineUserId()` prefers the in-memory `signedInUserId` but falls back to `localStorage.getItem(LAST_USER_KEY)` (offline-erase.ts:90-99). That in-memory value is set only by `rememberOfflineUser`, called from `OfflineRuntime`, which is mounted only under `PrivateRoute` (PrivateRoute.tsx). `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` (line 237) is reachable from `logout()` in api/auth.ts, which is callable from any route. In a tab that never mounted the authenticated shell — a signed-in user opening `/shared/:token` or `/t/:id` in a fresh tab on a shared machine — the fallback can return a previous account's id, so the erase targets that account while the current user's stored documents survive the sign-out. Confidence is low because reaching durable storage normally requires passing through `PrivateRoute`, which refreshes the mirror; I could not construct a sequence that both writes the current user's entries and leaves the mirror stale.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out in the repo. `durableClientKey` really does build the Yorkie client key as `wb:${userId}:${docKey}` (durable-session.ts:80-82) from fully guessable inputs: `String(me.id)` (collab-document-provider.tsx:205), a numeric user id published to all workspace members (api/workspaces.ts:23), plus a docKey derived from a document id visible in URLs. Tokens are cheap to obtain: `GET /auth/yorkie-token` for any account (auth.controller.ts:73-77) and the unauthenticated `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:87-95, no JwtAuthGuard). The durable path is reachable in production via the user-facing offline-persistence opt-in (settings/page.tsx:32). This is a missing authorization binding between the authenticated identity and a per-user server-side resource — in-lane (access control / IDOR), not a general correctness bug. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and the one unverifiable element (Yorkie server's ActivateClient upsert semantics) is exactly the behaviour the feature's own resume guarantee depends on, so doubt there argues for keeping the finding, not dropping it.

verdict.reason: The structural facts are as described — SharedDocumentInner returns SharedPdfLayout at shared-document.tsx:966-980, before the NonDurableScope wrapper at :1016, and SharedPdfLayout reaches PdfCollabProvider -> CollabDocumentProvider with docKey `pdf-${documentId}` (pdf-collab.tsx:199-200). However, the operation NonDurableScope protects is independently unreachable for that key. The sole durable client mount in the entire frontend is collab-document-provider.tsx:309-327, gated at :305 on `decided.durable`; that derives from useDurableDocument (:203), whose eligibility at use-durable-document.ts:127-132 requires `!isExcluded(docKey)`, and isExcluded returns true for any `pdf-` prefix (use-durable-document.ts:40-42). I grepped every DurableYorkieProvider and useDurableDocument call site — one each, both in collab-document-provider.tsx — so there is no alternate path. Consequently fetchYorkieToken (collab-document-provider.tsx:318) is never reached on the share PDF route; the mount stays on the share-token YorkieProvider (shared-document.tsx:753-758). The finding concedes this and premises its harm on a future removal of the pdf- exclusion described in a design document, not on code in this tree. That is a defense-in-depth/latent-fragility concern (worth a hardening note and PDF-branch test coverage), not a currently reachable authorization bypass or credential misuse under the Security rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: offline-runtime.tsx:114-142 swallows any reconcile failure (fetchDocuments reject, incl. the 401/AuthExpiredError arm) with a bare console.warn, and control falls through unconditionally to offerRecoverableWork at offline-runtime.tsx:150 — the only intervening check is `if (cancelled) return` (unmount, not reconcile success). offerRecoverableWork (offline-runtime.tsx:182-263) enumerates every archive via listRecoverableWork (offline-copy.ts:58-68 → store.listArchives(), no access filtering) and exposes a 'Save a copy' action that calls recoverOfflineCopy, which at offline-copy-recovery.ts:196-213 performs createDocument({title,type}) + applyImportedContent/writeNote with no access check, turning the archive into a durable server-side document owned by the current user. The repo's own documentation names this exact harm as the reason archives are dropped on revocation: offline-erase.ts:333-341 states purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments is the only mechanism reaching the removed member's device, and offline-erase.ts:355-358 / 394-398 say keeping an archive past revocation 'would hand them a permanent copy of content they may no longer read' and was previously fixed. purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments also swallows its own errors (offline-erase.ts:408-411), so no success signal exists for the caller to gate on. offline-runtime.test.tsx:177-183 asserts the toast still appears after fetchDocuments rejects, confirming the unguarded path is live. mergedFrom.summary: Revocation reconcile can never purge an archive: it enumerates candidates from HEADERS, and archiving deletes the header

finding.summary: Revocation reconcile cannot see archive-only documents, so content from a workspace the user was removed from is never erased
finding.evidence:
`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` builds its candidate list with `store.storedDocumentIds()` (offline-erase.ts:351), and that method enumerates only the `headers` object store (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:930-942, `headerKeysWhere(BY_USER, ...)`). But `remove()` deletes the header and writes the content into the separate `archives` store — so a document that hit `LocalChangesDropped` has an archive and NO header. It is therefore absent from `storedDocumentIds()`, `purgeDocument(id, {archives:'drop'})` is never called for it, and the archive survives the reconcile.

This is the exact case the design says the reconcile exists for. `workspaces.ts` removeMember documents that the removed member's own device "is reached by nothing that happens here, so it reconciles on its own: OfflineRuntime asks the server what it may still read on every session and drops what is no longer listed (purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments)". For an archived document that promise is not kept.

Chain: user A opens sheet-X in workspace W; the SDK hits one of the three LocalChangesDropped paths, so the full compressed document moves to `archives`. An owner removes A from W. On A's next session purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments sees no header for sheet-X and drops nothing. OfflineRuntime's recovery toast then offers the archive back and recoverOfflineCopy creates `sheet-X (offline copy)` — a permanent, server-side document A owns, containing content from a workspace A was removed from.

The existing test misses it because it re-seeds the live entry after archiving: offline-erase.test.ts "drops what the server no longer lists, archives included" calls store.remove(...) and then `await seed(store, "pk/wb:1:sheet-gone/sheet-gone")` again, restoring the header the real scenario would not have. The archive-only shape is untested.

Contrast showing the fix exists: deleteWorkspace/removeMember pass ids from the server listing, so purgeDocument reaches dropArchivesForDocument (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:945) regardless of hea

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted evidence does not match the repository. offline-erase.ts:396 calls `store.storedDocumentIds({ archives: true })`, not the header-only `storedDocumentIds()` the finding claims. wafflebase-doc-store.ts:937-956 shows `storedDocumentIds` takes `{archives?: boolean}` and, when set, appends `documentKeyOf(archive.docKey)` for every row from `listArchives()` (user-scoped, lines 986-997) — so an archive-only document (header deleted by `remove()`) IS in the candidate list. Each candidate is then purged with `archives: "drop"` (offline-erase.ts:400-406), and in `purgeDocument` the `options.archives === "drop"` branch at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:902-904 runs unconditionally after the header loop, so `dropArchivesForDocument` (line 959) is reached even when zero header keys matched; the `skipOpen`/`updatedSince` guards (lines 886-890) are inside the header loop and cannot spare the archive. The claim that the archive-only shape is untested is also false: offline-erase.test.ts:418-433 ("reaches a document that exists only as an archive") archives without re-seeding, asserts one archive exists, runs purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments, and asserts listArchives() is empty. The described revoked-access content-retention vector is not present as described.

finding.summary: Revocation reconcile bails out on an empty accessible list — exactly the shape a fully-revoked user produces
finding.evidence:
`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` returns 0 when `accessible.length === 0` (offline-erase.ts:339-344). The stated justification is "A user who genuinely has no documents has nothing stored either" — that reasoning is inverted for the one case this function exists to handle.

`GET /documents` (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180-195) returns documents across the caller's workspace memberships. A user whose stored offline copies all came from workspace W, and who is then removed from W, gets `[]` back on the next session if they hold no other documents. The guard then refuses to purge anything, so every local copy of W's documents — full document content they may no longer read — stays on the disk until the 30-day `collectStale` sweep. The same empty answer is also what a legitimately-revoked-from-everything user produces, so the guard cannot distinguish the safe case from the exact unsafe one.

The caller (`OfflineRuntime`, components/offline-runtime.tsx) already separates a *failed* listing (which throws before reaching here) from a successful empty one, so the successful-empty case could be honoured safely.

verdict.reason:
The finding claims `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` contains an early `return 0` when `accessible.length === 0`, at offline-erase.ts:339-344. That code is not present. The function is defined at offline-erase.ts:369-414 and its body has exactly one early return — `if (!who) return 0;` at lines 379-382 (no offline user identity). There is no length check on `accessible` anywhere in the function; `accessible` is used only at line 388 (`const keep = new Set(accessible)`) and lines 396-398 (filter stored ids not in `keep`). With an empty `accessible`, `keep` is empty and `revoked` becomes the entire stored set, so the function purges every local copy including archives (`archives: "drop"`, line 402) — the exact behavior the finding says is missing.

The cited lines 339-344 fall inside the doc comment spanning lines 333-368, not code. Lines 343-348 explicitly state the opposite of the finding: "`accessible` is the whole set the caller can read, and **an empty array is a valid answer** ... Refusing it — which this did — declined the reconcile precisely when it was owed, on the reasoning that a user with no documents has nothing stored, which is inverted here." The reviewer's quoted justification appears in the repository only as a past-tense description of a removed guard being rejected, and was mistaken for live code.

The caller contract is also already what the finding proposes: offline-runtime.tsx:133-139 stamps `listedAt`, awaits `fetchDocuments()`, and passes the ids through, while a failed listing throws into the catch at line 140 before the purge is invoked. Grep across packages/frontend/src confirms this is the only call site and the only definition, so no other path reintroduces the claimed guard.

mergedFrom.summary: `isOpenInAnyTab` matches a lock held by any account, so another user's open tab defers this user's revocation purge

finding.summary: isOpenInAnyTab fails open as "open" for the erasure callers, silently disabling both the revocation purge and the 30-day sweep on browsers with LockManager.request but no query
finding.evidence:
isOpenInAnyTab returns `true` — meaning "assume open, do not delete" — both when supportsDurableSession() is false (durable-session.ts:211-213) and when navigator.locks.query() throws (durable-session.ts:228-230). That default is correct for its original caller, eviction, where refusing to delete costs a failed write. It is inverted for the two erasure callers, where refusing to delete costs retained content the user is no longer entitled to.

Reachability is not hypothetical, because the capability probe and the call disagree about which API they need. supportsDurableSession() checks only `typeof navigator.locks.request === "function"` (durable-session.ts:57-65); it never probes `query`. On a runtime shipping LockManager.request but not LockManager.query, durability is ENABLED — entries and archives get written — while line 215 throws TypeError on every call and the catch answers `true` forever.

Consequences, both permanent on such a runtime:
- purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments passes `skipOpen: true` and `isOpenElsewhere: isOpenInAnyTab` (offline-erase.ts:356, offline-runtime.tsx), so purgeDocument's `if (options.skipOpen && (await this.isLive(key))) continue;` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:886) skips EVERY entry. Access revoked by someone else is never cleaned up.
- collectStale's isLive check skips every live entry for the same reason, so the 30-day backstop the design's cleanup table names as the catch-all for every other row never collects anything.

A transient query() rejection costs one sweep; the missing-query case costs all of them. Fix is to fail in the safe direction per caller — erasure should treat "cannot tell" as "not open" — or require `query` in supportsDurableSession() so durability is refused where the guard cannot work.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present. `isOpenInAnyTab` (packages/frontend/src/lib/durable-session.ts:227-260) does not hardcode `true` for the unknown case: it takes a `whenUnknown` option (`const unknown = options.whenUnknown ?? true;` line 231) and returns that caller-chosen value both from the capability check (line 237) and the catch (line 258). It also explicitly probes `typeof navigator.locks?.query !== "function"` (line 235), so the "LockManager.request but no query" runtime the finding builds its reachability argument on is detected directly rather than throwing a TypeError.
